q: Which white-marble Kolkata monument, opened in 1921, is dedicated to a British queen?
note: It sits on 64 acres of gardens and now serves as a museum.

q: In which year did Kolkata open India's first metro railway?
note: The first stretch ran just 3.4 km, from Esplanade to Bhowanipore.

q: In Bengali, which word means sweet, as in the dessert '___ doi'?
note: Mishti doi is sweetened yoghurt, traditionally set in earthen pots.

q: Joynagar in West Bengal is famous for which winter sweet made with nolen gur and puffed rice?
note: Joynagar's moa received a GI tag in 2015.

q: In Kolkata, what is a long, relaxed chat session with friends over tea called?
note: Kolkata's coffee houses, especially the one on College Street, are legendary adda spots.

q: Rabindranath Tagore founded Visva-Bharati University in which town?
note: Classes were often held outdoors under the trees.

q: Which Bengali poet is famously called the 'Bidrohi Kobi', or Rebel Poet?
note: He was born in Churulia, West Bengal, and is the national poet of Bangladesh.

q: What is the genre of songs written and composed by Rabindranath Tagore called?
note: Tagore wrote over 2,000 songs and set most of them to music himself.

q: Kolkata's biggest football rivalry, Mohun Bagan vs East Bengal, is popularly called what?
note: Mohun Bagan was founded in 1889 and East Bengal in 1920.

q: Which Bengali collection of nonsense verse was written by Sukumar Ray, Satyajit Ray's father?
note: It was first published in 1923 and is still a childhood favourite in Bengal.

q: The famous Bankura horse of West Bengal is made from what material?
note: The best-known Bankura horses come from the village of Panchmura.

q: What is the famous spiral loop of the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway near Ghum called?
note: The railway has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999.

q: Which viewpoint near Darjeeling is famous for sunrise views over Kanchenjunga?
note: On clear days, even Mount Everest can be spotted from there.

q: Kolkata's College Street, called 'Boi Para' by locals, is famous for what?
note: Boi Para means 'book neighbourhood'; its Indian Coffee House is iconic.

q: Which spicy puffed-rice street snack, tossed with mustard oil, is a Kolkata favourite?
note: 'Jhal' means spicy and 'muri' means puffed rice.

q: Which north Kolkata neighbourhood is famous for its clay idol makers?
note: Its name comes from 'kumor', the Bengali word for potter.

q: What is the Bengali New Year, celebrated in mid-April, called?
note: Shops open fresh account books called haal khata on this day.

q: Which was the first Indian Institute of Technology, set up in 1951?
note: It began in the old Hijli Detention Camp building.

q: What are the wandering mystic folk minstrels of Bengal called?
note: They usually carry a one-stringed instrument called the ektara.

q: Which antiseptic cream brand in a green tube was launched in Kolkata in 1929?
note: Its logo is an elephant, and the company is GD Pharmaceuticals.

q: Britannia, the biscuit company, was founded in 1892 in which city?
note: It reportedly began with an investment of just Rs 295.

q: What does the Bengali word 'bhalo' mean?
note: 'Bhalo achi' is the usual Bengali reply meaning 'I'm fine'.

q: Which Bengali festival is all about pampering sons-in-law with a lavish feast?
note: Mothers-in-law traditionally serve the jamai a spread of fish, sweets and mangoes.

q: What do Bengalis call the festival of Bhai Dooj?
note: Sisters place a sandalwood 'phonta' (dot) on their brothers' foreheads.

q: Which Tagore short story is about an Afghan dry-fruit seller's friendship with a little girl, Mini?
note: The story was first published in 1892.

q: Singer Arijit Singh hails from which town in West Bengal's Murshidabad district?
note: Jiaganj lies on the banks of the Bhagirathi river.

q: Which Everest pioneer was the first director of field training at Darjeeling's Himalayan Mountaineering Institute?
note: The institute was founded in 1954, a year after the first Everest ascent.

q: Which slow-cooked, dark and spicy Bengali mutton dish is a classic Sunday lunch?
note: 'Kosha' refers to slow frying the meat until the gravy turns thick and dark.

q: Kolkata's iconic yellow taxis have long been which classic Indian car model?
note: The Ambassador was built by Hindustan Motors at Uttarpara, near Kolkata.

q: European sailors used the Konark Sun Temple as a landmark and called it what?
note: The name came from the temple's dark appearance when seen from the sea.

q: Which Odia dish of cooked rice soaked in water has its own celebration day on 20 March?
note: It is especially loved in summer as a cooling meal.

q: Sambalpuri saris from Odisha use which technique, where the threads are tie-dyed before weaving?
note: Locally the technique is called 'bandha'.

q: Cuttack's famous tarakasi filigree craft is made mainly from which metal?
note: Cuttack is often nicknamed the 'Silver City' because of it.

q: The village of Pipili in Odisha is famous for which colourful textile craft?
note: The craft uses cut pieces of coloured cloth stitched onto a base fabric.

q: Odisha's Similipal Tiger Reserve is famous for which rare kind of tiger?
note: Their dark stripes are so broad and merged that they look almost black.

q: With help from which country was the Rourkela Steel Plant built in Odisha?
note: Production began there in 1959.

q: Legendary guru Kelucharan Mohapatra is associated with which classical dance?
note: He also performed as a percussionist on the mardala drum.

q: Which Bhubaneswar stadium hosted the 2018 men's Hockey World Cup?
note: Odisha co-hosted the 2023 edition too, with Rourkela's new stadium.

q: In which year was Odia declared a classical language of India?
note: Odia was the sixth language to get the status, after Malayalam.

q: Utkal Divas marks Odisha becoming a separate province on 1 April of which year?
note: The new province joined Odia-speaking areas of Bihar and Orissa Province and Madras Presidency.

q: Cuttack's Bali Jatra fair is named after an island in which present-day country?
note: It recalls the ancient Kalinga sailors who traded across Southeast Asia.

q: Which Puri artist is famous worldwide for his giant sand sculptures on the beach?
note: He received the Padma Shri in 2014.

q: Which three-day Odisha festival is famous for girls enjoying decorated rope swings?
note: It celebrates the earth and the arrival of the monsoon.

q: Nuakhai, the harvest festival of western Odisha, celebrates eating the first new what?
note: 'Nua' means new and 'khai' means eating.

q: Which tribal hero, revered as 'Dharti Aba', has his birth anniversary as Jharkhand's foundation day?
note: Jharkhand was formed on 15 November 2000, his birth anniversary.

q: In 2000, Jharkhand was carved out of which state?
note: Chhattisgarh and Uttarakhand were also created that same month.

q: Which city is cricketer MS Dhoni's hometown?
note: Before cricket took over, Dhoni played as a football goalkeeper at school.

q: Which archer from Ranchi became world No. 1 in women's recurve in 2012?
note: As a child she practised by shooting mangoes off trees with stones.

q: Which Jharkhand hill station is called the 'Queen of Chotanagpur'?
note: It is famous for its sunrise and sunset viewpoints.

q: Which Jharkhand city is known as the 'Coal Capital of India'?
note: It hosts IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, founded in 1926 as a mining school.

q: Sohrai and Khovar, GI-tagged mural art forms, come from which state?
note: Women paint them on mud walls of homes, mainly around Hazaribagh.

q: Sarhul, Jharkhand's spring festival, honours the blossoms of which tree?
note: It marks the new year for several tribal communities of the region.

q: Dhuska, a deep-fried rice-and-lentil bread, is a popular breakfast in which state?
note: It is often eaten with a spicy potato-and-chickpea curry.

q: What is the highest peak in Jharkhand?
note: It rises over 1,300 metres and is a major Jain pilgrimage site.

q: The name Jharkhand literally means 'land of' what?
note: Much of the state lies on the forested Chota Nagpur Plateau.

q: Which Assamese silk is called 'peace silk' because the silkworm is not killed?
note: The moth leaves the cocoon before the silk is spun.

q: What is the white handwoven Assamese cloth with a red border, offered as a mark of respect?
note: The Assam gamosa got a GI tag in 2022.

q: Which buffalo-horn pipe is a signature instrument of Bihu music?
note: It is played alongside the dhol and the gogona, a bamboo mouth harp.

q: The January harvest Bihu, famous for feasts and bonfires, is called Magh Bihu or what?
note: The night before, called Uruka, is spent feasting in makeshift huts.

q: The National Defence Academy's best-cadet gold medal is named after which Ahom general?
note: Assam celebrates Lachit Divas on 24 November.

q: The Rang Ghar, an Ahom royal pavilion for watching sports, stands in which Assam town?
note: Its roof is shaped like an upturned royal Ahom boat.

q: Which tangy Assamese fish curry is soured with tomato or lemon?
note: 'Tenga' means sour in Assamese.

q: Til pitha, a Bihu snack of rice-flour rolls, is filled with sesame and what?
note: The rolls are made on a flat pan using sticky bora rice.

q: What is the Assamese bell-metal offering tray on a stand, used to honour guests?
note: Sarthebari in lower Assam is famous for its bell-metal craft.

q: What is the traditional Assamese conical hat made of bamboo and palm leaves called?
note: Decorated japis are hung on walls and gifted to honour guests.

q: Which Assam city is popularly called the 'Gateway to the Northeast'?
note: It sits on the banks of the Brahmaputra.

q: Which 15th-16th century Assamese saint-scholar is credited with creating the Ankiya Naat form of one-act plays?
note: He was born in 1449 in present-day Nagaon district.

q: Digboi in Assam is famous for which industrial site, running there since 1901?
note: It is one of the oldest operating oil refineries in the world.

q: Which Assam village is famous as the 'Manchester of the East' for silk weaving?
note: Almost every household there has a traditional handloom.

q: What is the traditional Assamese breakfast of flattened rice, curd and jaggery called?
note: It is especially popular during Bihu mornings.

q: Jnanpith Award-winning writer Indira Goswami wrote mainly in which language?
note: She also wrote under the pen name Mamoni Raisom Goswami.

q: Assam's Jonbeel Mela is famous as a fair where goods are exchanged how?
note: Hill and plains communities have traded this way there for centuries.

q: Kopou phool, Assam's state flower, is what kind of flower?
note: Bihu dancers traditionally wear kopou phool in their hair.

q: Meghalaya's living root bridges are grown from the roots of which tree?
note: The roots are guided across streams by hand over many years.

q: Which Meghalaya village is famous for its double-decker living root bridge?
note: Reaching it means a trek down thousands of stone steps from Tyrna village.

q: Which Meghalaya village was dubbed 'Asia's cleanest village' in 2003?
note: The title came from Discover India magazine; villagers use bamboo dustbins.

q: Meghalaya's three main hill regions are the Khasi Hills, Jaintia Hills and which?
note: Each is named after the main community living there.

q: Which crystal-clear river at Dawki makes boats look like they are floating in air?
note: In winter the water is clear enough to see the riverbed below.

q: Which Meghalaya cave is the longest natural cave known in India?
note: It lies in the Jaintia Hills and stretches for over 30 km.

q: Which choir from Meghalaya won India's Got Talent in 2010?
note: The choir was founded by pianist and composer Neil Nongkynrih.

q: Nohkalikai Falls, one of India's tallest plunge waterfalls, is near which rain-soaked town?
note: The falls drop about 340 metres into a green pool.

q: In traditional Khasi families, who usually inherits the ancestral property?
note: The Khasi follow a matrilineal system, with children taking the mother's clan name.

q: Wangala, the Garo harvest festival, is popularly called the festival of how many drums?
note: It honours Saljong, the sun god of fertility.

q: Which Khasi dish of rice cooked with pork is a Meghalaya signature?
note: It is often eaten as a hearty breakfast in Shillong.

q: What is polo traditionally called in Manipur, where the modern game took shape?
note: Imphal's Mapal Kangjeibung is often called the world's oldest polo ground.

q: Which martial art of Manipur combines the sword and the spear?
note: 'Thang' means sword and 'Ta' means spear.

q: The Manipuri classical dance is best known for which dance-drama about Radha and Krishna?
note: Dancers wear a stiff, drum-shaped embroidered skirt called the potloi.

q: Imphal's Ima Keithel market is famously run entirely by whom?
note: The name means 'Mothers' Market' and it has thousands of stalls.

q: Which Manipuri boxer won bantamweight gold at the 1998 Bangkok Asian Games?
note: He inspired a generation of boxers, including Mary Kom.

q: Ngari, a key ingredient in Manipuri cooking, is fermented what?
note: It flavours eromba, a spicy mash of vegetables and chilli.

q: What is Manipur's GI-tagged aromatic black rice called?
note: It turns deep purple when cooked and is used in kheer.

q: Which historic fort by the Imphal River was the seat of Manipur's kings?
note: Two large white dragon-like statues called kangla sha guard it.

q: Which rare lily, Manipur's state flower, grows wild only on hills in Ukhrul district?
note: It blooms in pale pink between May and June.

q: What is Manipur's five-day spring festival, like Holi and famous for sports events, called?
note: Children collect money door to door and play games at night.

q: Which Manipuri dance is performed acrobatically by dancers while playing drums?
note: The 'pung' is a barrel-shaped drum central to Manipuri music.

q: Mizoram's Cheraw dance is performed by stepping between moving poles of what?
note: Men clap the poles together while women dance nimbly in and out.

q: Which Mizo spring festival celebrates finishing the clearing of jungle for farming?
note: 'Kut' means festival in Mizo.

q: The Mizo language is written in which script?
note: The Roman-letter Mizo alphabet was devised in the 1890s.

q: Phawngpui, Mizoram's highest peak, is also known as what?
note: It rises about 2,157 metres near the Myanmar border.

q: Which club from Mizoram won the 2016-17 I-League?
note: It was the first club from the Northeast to win India's top league.

q: What is the traditional handwoven Mizo wraparound skirt called?
note: The colourful puanchei is worn for festivals and weddings.

q: The name Mizoram literally means 'land of the' whom?
note: 'Mi' means people, 'zo' means hill and 'ram' means land.

q: What is the name of Mizoram's highest waterfall, near Thenzawl?
note: It plunges roughly 750 feet in two tiers through thick forest.

q: In Mizo, what does 'Ka lawm e' mean?
note: Mizo is widely spoken in Mizoram and parts of neighbouring states.

q: In which year did Nagaland become a state of India?
note: It became India's 16th state.

q: What is Nagaland's state bird, a colourful Himalayan pheasant?
note: Males puff out a bright yellow throat flap during courtship.

q: Which semi-wild bovine is the state animal of both Nagaland and Arunachal Pradesh?
note: Mithuns are a traditional symbol of wealth in many hill communities.

q: Which Assamese-based creole serves as a common tongue across Nagaland?
note: It helps speakers of many different Naga languages talk to each other.

q: What is the official language of Nagaland?
note: Nagaland adopted English as its official language in 1967.

q: What is a traditional Naga communal house for village youth called?
note: Morungs were places to learn crafts, folklore, songs and discipline.

q: In Nagaland's Longwa village, the chief's house sits across India's border with which country?
note: Villagers joke that the chief eats in India and sleeps in Myanmar.

q: In which event did Nagaland's Hokato Hotozhe Sema win Paralympic bronze at Paris 2024?
note: He competed in the F57 category.

q: Sekrenyi is the main festival of which Naga tribe?
note: It is held in February and is a festival of purification.

q: Which ingredient is famously cooked with pork in Naga cuisine?
note: Fermented bamboo shoot gives Naga dishes their distinctive tangy aroma.

q: Which white royal palace in Agartala now houses the Tripura State Museum?
note: It was completed around 1901 by Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya.

q: Tripura's water palace, Neermahal, stands in the middle of which lake?
note: It was built in the 1930s as a summer palace for Tripura's royal family.

q: Unakoti in Tripura is famous for giant ancient what?
note: Some of the carved faces are several metres tall.

q: Music composer S.D. Burman was a prince of which royal family?
note: His son R.D. Burman became one of Bollywood's most loved composers.

q: Besides Bengali, what is the main indigenous language of Tripura?
note: 'Kok' means language and 'borok' means people.

q: Hojagiri, a dance performed while balancing on earthen pots, comes from which state?
note: Dancers also balance bottles and lamps on their heads while moving.

q: Tripura's GI-tagged 'Queen' variety is which fruit?
note: It is known for its sweet aroma and golden-yellow flesh.

q: Which Arunachal Pradesh town is home to a 17th-century monastery often called the largest in India?
note: The monastery sits at about 3,000 metres above sea level.

q: Which Arunachal valley, home of the Apatani people, hosts a famous outdoor music festival?
note: The Ziro Festival of Music began in 2012.

q: Dree, an agricultural festival held in July, belongs to which Arunachal community?
note: Prayers are offered for a good harvest and protection of crops.

q: Sangestar Tso lake near Tawang is popularly named after which Bollywood actress?
note: A song from the 1997 film Koyla was shot at the lake.

q: Which state is known as the 'Orchid State of India'?
note: The state is home to over 500 species of orchids.

q: Which Arunachal mountaineer climbed Everest twice within five days in 2017?
note: She is a mother of two from Bomdila.

q: Before 1972, Arunachal Pradesh was known by which four-letter acronym?
note: It was renamed Arunachal Pradesh in 1972 and became a full state in 1987.

q: In which year did Sikkim become a state of India?
note: Sikkim became India's 22nd state on 16 May 1975.

q: In 2016, Sikkim was declared India's first fully what state?
note: Chemical fertilisers and pesticides were phased out across the state's farms.

q: Gurudongmar, one of India's highest lakes, is in which state?
note: It lies in North Sikkim and is a source stream of the Teesta.

q: Which Sikkim festival honours Mount Kanchenjunga as a guardian deity?
note: The festival features colourful masked chaam dances.

q: Gundruk, a staple in Sikkim, is made from fermented what?
note: Mustard, radish and cauliflower leaves are commonly used.

q: What is the rock-hard cheese that people in Sikkim chew for hours called?
note: It is made from yak or cow milk and dried until very hard.

q: Which steamed dumpling with Tibetan roots is a street-food favourite in Sikkim and Darjeeling?
note: They are usually served with a fiery red tomato-and-chilli chutney.

q: Bollywood actor Danny Denzongpa hails from which state?
note: He trained at the Film and Television Institute of India in Pune.

q: The northeastern states are called the 'Seven Sisters'; Sikkim is nicknamed what?
note: Sikkim joined the North Eastern Council in 2002.

q: Havelock Island, home of Radhanagar Beach, was renamed what in 2018?
note: Radhanagar was named Asia's best beach by Time magazine in 2004.

q: Neil Island in the Andamans was renamed what in 2018?
note: Ross Island was renamed Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Dweep at the same time.

q: The natural rock arch on Neil Island is nicknamed after which famous bridge?
note: The arch formed from coral rock and is best seen at low tide.

q: Which bird, found in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, is the closest living relative of the extinct dodo?
note: Its shimmering green-and-copper feathers make it one of the most colourful pigeons.
